section.title: Ara denemeler
section.description: Planın 22., 24. ve 27. haftaları: o ana kadarki konulardan karışık tekrar, ardından 40 soruluk yarım deneme

units.title: Ara tekrar 1
units.description: Yarım deneme 2 öncesi karışık tekrar: dilbilgisi, cloze, çeviri, okuma ve paragraf soruları
units.guide:
## Bu haftaya kadar gördüğün soru tipleri
- **Kelime ve dilbilgisi:** zamanlar, kipler, edilgen yapı, koşul cümleleri, sıfat cümleleri, bağlaçlar
- **Cloze ve cümle tamamlama:** boşluğun öncesine ve sonrasına bakarak yapı ve anlam seçme
- **Çeviri:** İngilizce–Türkçe ve Türkçe–İngilizce, öğe öğe karşılaştırma
- **Okuma:** ana fikir, ayrıntı, çıkarım, gönderim (*it, which*) ve yazarın tutumu
- **Diyalog, yakın anlam, paragraf tamamlama, anlamı bozan cümle**

Bu ünite bir dedektif gibi çalışmanı istiyor: her sorunun cevabını metindeki bir **ipucuna** dayandır.

## Yarım deneme için zaman planı (90 dakika)
- Kelime ve dilbilgisi: **20 dk**
- Cloze ve cümle tamamlama: **25 dk**
- Okuma: **30 dk**
- Çeviri, diyalog ve paragraf soruları: **15 dk**

Bir soruda 2 dakikadan fazla kalırsan işaretle ve geç; sona kalan sürede geri dön.

## Denemeden sonra
- Her yanlışın nedenini **Hata defteri**ne yaz: kelimeyi mi bilmedin, yapıyı mı kaçırdın, süre mi yetmedi?
- En çok yanlış yaptığın soru tipini seç ve o tipin dersini yeniden çöz.
- Doğru yaptığın ama tahmin ettiğin soruların açıklamalarını da yeniden oku.

nodes.title: Dilbilgisi ve cloze
nodes.description: Ağaç halkalarıyla tarihleme üzerine bir cloze metni ve dedektif hikâyelerinden dilbilgisi soruları

exercises.passage: When a wooden object is found at an old site, investigators often want to know exactly when the tree it came from was cut down. Dendrochronology, the study of tree rings, (1)---- them to answer this question with surprising accuracy. Every year a tree adds a new ring, and the width of that ring depends on the weather: in wet years the rings are wide, (2)---- in dry years they are narrow. Because all the trees in a region experience the same weather, they share the same pattern of wide and narrow rings. By matching samples from living trees with older beams and posts, researchers (3)---- a continuous record that, in some parts of Europe, now goes back more than ten thousand years. A single wooden beam can therefore (4)---- to the exact year in which its tree stopped growing. If the outer ring is still present, scientists can even tell (5)---- the tree was felled in spring or in autumn.
exercises.question: (1) numaralı boşluk için en uygun ifadeyi seçin.
options: enables
prevents
avoids
suggests
insists
exercises.explanation: Boşluktan sonra ‘them to answer’ geliyor; ‘enable somebody to do’ (birinin bir şeyi yapmasını sağlamak) kalıbı ve anlam buna uyar. ‘prevents’ ‘from + -ing’ ister ve anlamı tersine çevirir; ‘avoids’ ‘-ing’ alır, nesne + to almaz; ‘suggests’ ve ‘insists’ de ‘somebody to do’ yapısıyla kullanılmaz.

exercises.question: (2) numaralı boşluk için en uygun ifadeyi seçin.
options: because
whereas
so that
unless
as if
exercises.explanation: Islak yıllarda halkaların geniş, kurak yıllarda dar olduğu söyleniyor; iki durumu karşılaştıran bağlaç ‘whereas’ (oysa, -iken) gerekir. ‘because’ neden bildirir, burada neden-sonuç yok; ‘so that’ amaç bildirir; ‘unless’ koşul kurar; ‘as if’ (-mış gibi) ise benzetme yapar ve anlamı bozar.

exercises.question: (3) numaralı boşluk için en uygun ifadeyi seçin.
options: had constructed
will construct
were constructed
have constructed
had been constructing
exercises.explanation: Kayıt bugün (‘now goes back’) on bin yılı aşıyor; geçmişte başlayıp sonucu şimdiye uzanan iş için present perfect gerekir: ‘have constructed’. ‘had constructed’ ve ‘had been constructing’ geçmişteki başka bir ana göre önceliği anlatır, burada böyle bir an yok; ‘will construct’ işi geleceğe atar ve ‘now goes back’ ile çelişir; ‘were constructed’ edilgendir, oysa özne olan araştırmacılar işi kendileri yapar.

exercises.question: (4) numaralı boşluk için en uygun ifadeyi seçin.
options: be traced
trace
have traced
tracing
been tracing
exercises.explanation: Kirişin kendisi bir şeyi izlemez, bir yıla kadar izlenir; ‘can’ yardımcı fiilinden sonra edilgen yalın biçim gerekir: ‘be traced’. ‘trace’ ve ‘have traced’ etken yapıdır ve nesnesiz kalır; ‘tracing’ ve ‘been tracing’ ise ‘can’ ile kullanılamaz.

exercises.passage: When a wooden object is found at an old site, investigators often want to know exactly when the tree it came from was cut down. Dendrochronology, the study of tree rings, (1)---- them to answer this question with surprising accuracy. Every year a tree adds a new ring, and the width of that ring depends on the weather: in wet years the rings are wide, (2)---- in dry years they are narrow. Because all the trees in a region experience the same weather, they share the same pattern of wide and narrow rings. A single wooden beam can therefore (4)---- to the exact year in which its tree stopped growing. exercises.question: (5) numaralı boşluk için en uygun ifadeyi seçin.
options: unless
although
since
despite
whether
exercises.explanation: ‘in spring or in autumn’ iki seçenek sunuyor; ‘tell whether … or …’ (… mı yoksa … mı olduğunu anlamak) kalıbı gerekir: ‘whether’. ‘unless’ (-mezse) koşul, ‘although’ (-e rağmen) karşıtlık, ‘since’ (-den beri/çünkü) neden bildirir; ‘despite’ ise ardından cümle değil isim ister.

exercises.question: The detective who interviewed the three witnesses on Monday ---- that none of their stories matched.
options: realising
realised
to realise
having realised
who realised
exercises.explanation: Cümlenin öznesi ‘The detective’; ‘who interviewed … on Monday’ araya giren sıfat cümlesidir. Ana cümlenin çekimli bir fiile ihtiyacı var: ‘realised’. ‘realising’ ve ‘having realised’ fiilimsidir, yüklem olamaz; ‘to realise’ da tek başına yüklem değildir; ‘who realised’ ise ikinci bir sıfat cümlesi kurar ve cümleyi yine yüklemsiz bırakır.

exercises.question: If the guard ---- the back door before leaving, the thief would not have entered the building so easily.
options: has locked
locks
would lock
had locked
was locking
exercises.explanation: Ana cümledeki ‘would not have entered’ geçmişe dair gerçek dışı bir durumu (üçüncü tip koşul) anlatır; ‘if’ cümlesinde past perfect gerekir: ‘had locked’. ‘has locked’ ve ‘locks’ birinci tip koşula aittir; ‘would lock’ ‘if’ cümlesinde kullanılmaz; ‘was locking’ ise süregiden bir eylem bildirir ve kalıba uymaz.

exercises.question: The footprints in the garden are far too small for an adult, so they ---- by the suspect, who is nearly two metres tall.
options: can't have been left
must have been left
should have left
might leave
had to leave
exercises.explanation: İzler bir yetişkine göre çok küçük, şüpheli ise çok uzun; geçmişe dair güçlü bir olumsuz çıkarım gerekir ve izler bırakılan şeydir (edilgen): ‘can't have been left’. ‘must have been left’ tam tersi bir çıkarım yapar; ‘should have left’ eleştiri bildirir ve etkendir; ‘might leave’ geleceğe dönük bir olasılıktır; ‘had to leave’ ise zorunluluk bildirir ve anlamı bozar.

exercises.question: The woman ---- car was seen near the bank that night has finally agreed to speak to the police.
options: who
which
whose
whom
where
exercises.explanation: Boşluktan sonra gelen ‘car’ kadına aittir (kadının arabası); iyelik bildiren ilgi zamiri ‘whose’ gerekir. ‘who’ ve ‘whom’ ardından doğrudan isim almaz; ‘which’ insan için kullanılmaz; ‘where’ ise yer bildirir.

exercises.question: Since the museum reopened, all of its paintings ---- by hidden cameras day and night.
options: have watched
are watching
watched
had watched
have been watched
exercises.explanation: ‘Since the museum reopened’ geçmişten bugüne uzanan bir süreyi gösterir ve tabloları kameralar izler (tablolar izlenir); present perfect edilgen gerekir: ‘have been watched’. ‘have watched’, ‘are watching’, ‘watched’ ve ‘had watched’ etken yapılardır; tabloları izleyen özne yapar, ayrıca ‘had watched’ ve ‘watched’ ‘since’ ile zaman uyumunu da bozar.

exercises.question: The ---- of the stolen jewels in the owner's own garden made the police doubt his story.
options: discover
discovery
discovered
discoverable
discovers
exercises.explanation: ‘The … of the stolen jewels’ yapısında artikelden sonra ve ‘of’tan önce bir isim gerekir: ‘discovery’ (bulunma, keşif). ‘discover’ ve ‘discovers’ fiildir; ‘discovered’ fiilin geçmiş biçimidir; ‘discoverable’ ise sıfattır ve tek başına özne olamaz.

exercises.question: By the time the police arrived at the house, the burglars ----.
options: have already escaped
already escape
will already escape
had already escaped
are already escaping
exercises.explanation: ‘By the time’ + geçmiş zaman (‘arrived’) ana cümlede o andan önce tamamlanmış bir eylem ister: past perfect ‘had already escaped’. ‘have already escaped’ şimdiye bağlanır; ‘already escape’ geniş zamandır; ‘will already escape’ geleceği, ‘are already escaping’ ise şu anı anlatır; hiçbiri geçmişteki ‘arrived’ ile uyuşmaz.

nodes.title: Cümle tamamlama ve çeviri
nodes.description: Koşul, bağlaç ve sıfat cümleleriyle tamamlama; iki yönlü çeviri soruları

exercises.question: Although the suspect claimed he had been at home all evening, ----.
options: a neighbour had seen him leaving his flat at nine o'clock
so he was arrested the following morning
because his alibi was confirmed by his wife
which the police found very convincing
unless the neighbours tell the truth
exercises.explanation: ‘Although’ karşıtlık kurar: şüpheli bütün akşam evde olduğunu söylese de bir komşu onu saat dokuzda dairesinden çıkarken görmüştü (‘a neighbour had seen him leaving …’). ‘so he was arrested’ ‘although’ ile birlikte iki bağlaç kullanır; ‘alibi was confirmed’ karşıtlık değil destek bildirir; ‘convincing’ ile biten seçenek ana cümle değildir; ‘unless the neighbours’ ise ana cümle kurmaz ve zamanı bozar.

exercises.question: If the bank had installed better cameras, ----.
options: the robbers will be caught tomorrow
the robbers are identified within hours
the robbers would have been identified much sooner
although nobody had been hurt
whose faces were hidden by masks
exercises.explanation: ‘If … had installed’ üçüncü tip koşuldur; ana cümle ‘would have + V3’ ister: ‘the robbers would have been identified much sooner’. ‘will be caught tomorrow’ birinci tipe, ‘are identified within hours’ geniş zamana aittir; ‘although nobody had been hurt’ ve ‘whose faces were hidden’ ise ana cümle değildir.

exercises.question: The detective, ----, refused to close the case until every question had been answered.
options: which the newspapers had criticised
that he had never met before
was known for his patience
having been closed for years
who had worked for the police for thirty years
exercises.explanation: Virgüller arasındaki ek bilgi bir kişiyi (‘The detective’) niteleyen sıfat cümlesi ister: ‘who had worked for the police for thirty years’. ‘which the newspapers’ insan için ‘which’ kullanır; ‘that he had never met’ virgüllü cümlede ‘that’ kullanır ve anlamsızdır; ‘was known for his patience’ ilgi zamiri olmadan ikinci bir yüklem kurar; ‘having been closed’ ise dedektifin kapatıldığını söyler.

exercises.question: ----, the police were unable to charge him with the crime.
options: Even though the suspect had confessed to everything
Since there was no clear evidence against the suspect
As soon as fingerprints are found at the scene
So that the suspect could not escape
Whereas the witnesses will describe the man
exercises.explanation: Polisin suçlama yapamamasının nedeni gerekir: ‘Since there was no clear evidence against the suspect’. ‘confessed to everything’ itirafla sonucu çelişkili kılar; ‘As soon as fingerprints are found’ şimdiki/gelecek zaman kurar; ‘So that … could not escape’ amaç bildirir ve anlamsızdır; ‘Whereas the witnesses will describe’ ise zaman ve anlam olarak uymaz.

exercises.question: Unless the stolen painting is found within a week, ----.
options: the owner would have been delighted
the museum had already reopened
because the thief has left the country
the insurance company will have to pay the owner
which most experts consider unlikely
exercises.explanation: ‘Unless’ ile kurulan birinci tip koşul ana cümlede ‘will’ ister: ‘the insurance company will have to pay the owner’. ‘would have been delighted’ üçüncü tipe aittir; ‘had already reopened’ geçmişte kalır; ‘because the thief’ ve ‘which most experts’ ise ana cümle değildir.

exercises.question: The letter was written so carefully that ----.
options: even experienced experts could not tell it was a forgery
the forger had used cheap paper and a blue pen
nobody believed it was genuine
although the signature looked strange
whose author was never found
exercises.explanation: ‘so … that’ bir sonucu bildirir: mektup o kadar özenli yazılmıştı ki deneyimli uzmanlar bile sahte olduğunu anlayamadı (‘even experienced experts could not tell …’). ‘cheap paper’ özenin sonucu değildir; ‘nobody believed it was genuine’ özenli yazımla çelişir; ‘although the signature’ ve ‘whose author’ ise ‘that’tan sonra tam bir sonuç cümlesi kurmaz.

exercises.question:
Aşağıdaki İngilizce cümlenin anlamca en yakın Türkçe karşılığı hangisidir?

The stolen necklace, which had been missing for ten years, was finally found in a second-hand shop.
options: On yıl önce ikinci el bir dükkândan çalınan kolye hâlâ bulunamadı.
Çalıntı kolye on yıl boyunca ikinci el bir dükkânda satışta kaldı.
On yıldır kayıp olan çalıntı kolye sonunda ikinci el bir dükkânda bulundu.
Kolyeyi çalan kişi on yıl sonra ikinci el bir dükkânda yakalandı.
Kayıp kolyenin on yıl içinde birkaç kez satıldığı ortaya çıktı.
exercises.explanation: ‘which had been missing for ten years’ (on yıldır kayıp olan) ve ‘was finally found’ (sonunda bulundu) öğeleri ‘…sonunda ikinci el bir dükkânda bulundu.’ cümlesindedir. ‘hâlâ bulunamadı’ anlamı tersine çevirir; ‘satışta kaldı’ ve ‘birkaç kez satıldığı’ cümlede olmayan bilgiler ekler; ‘yakalandı’ ise kolyeyi değil hırsızı konu eder.

exercises.question:
Aşağıdaki İngilizce cümlenin anlamca en yakın Türkçe karşılığı hangisidir?

Had the witness not called the police, the thief might have escaped with the money.
options: Tanık polisi aradığı için hırsız parayı bırakıp kaçtı.
Tanık polisi aramadı, bu yüzden hırsız parayla kaçtı.
Hırsız parayla kaçarken tanık polisi aramaya çalıştı.
Tanık polisi arasa bile hırsız parayla kaçmayı başaracaktı.
Tanık polisi aramamış olsaydı hırsız parayla birlikte kaçabilirdi.
exercises.explanation: ‘Had the witness not called’ devrik üçüncü tip koşuldur (aramamış olsaydı); ‘might have escaped’ gerçekleşmemiş bir olasılıktır (kaçabilirdi): ‘Tanık polisi aramamış olsaydı …’. ‘bırakıp kaçtı’ ve ‘aramadı, bu yüzden’ olayları gerçekleşmiş gibi anlatır; ‘kaçarken … çalıştı’ koşulu yok eder; ‘arasa bile’ ise anlamı tersine çevirir.

exercises.question:
Aşağıdaki İngilizce cümlenin anlamca en yakın Türkçe karşılığı hangisidir?

It is thought that the fire was started deliberately to destroy important documents.
options: Yangında önemli belgelerin kazara yok olduğu düşünülüyor.
Yangının önemli belgeleri yok etmek için kasıtlı olarak çıkarıldığı düşünülüyor.
Önemli belgeler, yangın çıkmadan önce bilerek başka bir yere taşınmıştı.
Yangını kimin çıkardığı bilinmese de belgelerin kurtarıldığı düşünülüyor.
Önemli belgeleri yok etmek isteyenlerin yangın çıkarmayı planladığı kesin olarak biliniyor.
exercises.explanation: ‘It is thought that’ (… düşünülüyor), ‘deliberately’ (kasıtlı olarak) ve ‘to destroy’ (yok etmek için) öğeleri ‘…kasıtlı olarak çıkarıldığı düşünülüyor.’ cümlesindedir. ‘kazara’ kasıt anlamını tersine çevirir; ‘taşınmıştı’ ve ‘kurtarıldığı’ cümlede olmayan bilgiler verir; ‘kesin olarak biliniyor’ ise ‘is thought’ kesinsizliğini yok eder.

exercises.question:
Aşağıdaki Türkçe cümlenin anlamca en yakın İngilizce karşılığı hangisidir?

Dedektif, kasanın şifresini bilen tek kişinin müdür olduğunu fark etti.
options: The detective realised that the manager had forgotten the code of the safe.
The manager told the detective that only one person knew the code of the safe.
The detective wondered whether the manager knew anyone who could open the safe.
The detective realised that the manager was the only person who knew the code of the safe.
The detective knew the code of the safe because the manager had given it to him.
exercises.explanation: ‘şifresini bilen tek kişinin müdür olduğunu fark etti’ öğesi ‘…the manager was the only person who knew the code of the safe.’ cümlesinde karşılanır. ‘forgotten’ şifrenin unutulduğunu söyler; ‘told’ ile kurulan cümlede fark eden değil anlatan müdürdür; ‘wondered’ fark etmeyi merak etmeye çevirir; ‘given’ ise şifreyi dedektife verir.

exercises.question:
Aşağıdaki Türkçe cümlenin anlamca en yakın İngilizce karşılığı hangisidir?

Kamera kayıtları incelenmeseydi, gerçek suçlu asla bulunamayacaktı.
options: If the camera recordings had not been examined, the real criminal would never have been found.
If the camera recordings are examined, the real criminal will soon be found.
Although the camera recordings were examined, the real criminal was never found.
The real criminal was found before the camera recordings were examined.
The camera recordings showed that the real criminal had never been to the building.
exercises.explanation: ‘incelenmeseydi … bulunamayacaktı’ geçmişe dair gerçek dışı bir koşuldur; üçüncü tip koşul gerekir: ‘If the camera recordings had not been examined, … would never have been found.’ ‘will soon’ birinci tip koşul kurar; ‘Although … never found’ suçlunun bulunmadığını söyler; ‘before’ ile kurulan cümle sıralamayı tersine çevirir; ‘building’ ise cümlede olmayan bir bina bilgisi ekler.

exercises.question:
Aşağıdaki Türkçe cümlenin anlamca en yakın İngilizce karşılığı hangisidir?

Hırsızın içeri girmek için kullandığı merdiven bahçede bulundu.
options: The thief discovered a ladder in the garden and climbed it to get in.
The ladder in the garden was too short for the thief to get in.
The ladder which the thief used to get in was found in the garden.
The thief who was caught in the garden had used a ladder.
Someone had hidden the ladder in the garden before the thief got in.
exercises.explanation: ‘hırsızın içeri girmek için kullandığı merdiven’ bir sıfat cümlesiyle karşılanır ve bulunan şey merdivendir: ‘The ladder which the thief used to get in was found in the garden.’ ‘discovered … climbed’ merdiveni bulanı hırsız yapar; ‘too short’ cümlede olmayan bir bilgi ekler; ‘who was caught’ bahçede yakalananı hırsız yapar; ‘hidden’ ise saklama bilgisi ekler.

nodes.title: Okuma
nodes.description: Bir sahte tablo davası ve çölde kendi kendine yürüyen taşlar: iki uzun metin

exercises.passage: In 1945, shortly after the end of the Second World War, Dutch police arrested a painter named Han van Meegeren. He was accused of selling a valuable painting by the seventeenth-century master Johannes Vermeer to a senior Nazi official, which was considered an act of treason. To everyone's surprise, van Meegeren made a remarkable confession: the painting was not a Vermeer at all, because he had painted it himself. At first, few people believed him. Several respected experts had examined his "Vermeers" and declared them genuine, and one of them had been bought by a leading Dutch museum. To prove his claim, van Meegeren agreed to paint a new "Vermeer" in front of witnesses. Even so, the case was not settled until scientists examined the paintings in a laboratory. They discovered that he had mixed his paints with a modern plastic called Bakelite, which becomes hard when it is heated. This allowed the paint to dry within hours and look as hard and cracked as three-hundred-year-old paint. The scientists also found traces of a blue pigment that was not invented until more than a century after Vermeer's death. Van Meegeren was found guilty of forgery rather than treason and received a one-year sentence, but he died before he could serve it. In a strange way, he became something of a popular hero, since many people enjoyed the idea that he had fooled the Nazis. His story also taught museums an uncomfortable lesson: an expert's eye, however well trained, can be deceived when it wants to see a masterpiece.
exercises.question: The passage is mainly concerned with ----.
options: why Vermeer's paintings became so valuable after the Second World War
how Nazi officials collected paintings from Dutch museums during the war
the methods modern museums use to protect their paintings from theft
the life and works of the seventeenth-century painter Johannes Vermeer
how a forger's confession and scientific tests showed that some famous "Vermeers" were fake
exercises.explanation: Parça van Meegeren'in itirafını ve laboratuvar testlerinin tabloların sahte olduğunu nasıl kanıtladığını anlatır: ‘how a forger's confession and scientific tests showed …’. Tabloların neden değerlendiği (‘valuable’) ve Nazilerin tablo toplaması (‘collected’) yalnızca arka plandır; hırsızlığa karşı koruma (‘theft’) parçada yoktur; Vermeer'in hayatı (‘life and works’) ise anlatılmaz.

exercises.passage: In 1945, shortly after the end of the Second World War, Dutch police arrested a painter named Han van Meegeren. He was accused of selling a valuable painting by the seventeenth-century master Johannes Vermeer to a senior Nazi official, which was considered an act of treason. To everyone's surprise, van Meegeren made a remarkable confession: the painting was not a Vermeer at all, because he had painted it himself. At first, few people believed him. Several respected experts had examined his "Vermeers" and declared them genuine, and one of them had been bought by a leading Dutch museum. To prove his claim, van Meegeren agreed to paint a new "Vermeer" in front of witnesses. Even so, the case was not settled until scientists examined the paintings in a laboratory. They discovered that he had mixed his paints with a modern plastic called Bakelite, which becomes hard when it is heated. This allowed the paint to dry within hours and look as hard and cracked as three-hundred-year-old paint. The scientists also found traces of a blue pigment that was not invented until more than a century after Vermeer's death. Van Meegeren was found guilty of forgery rather than treason and received a one-year sentence, but he died before he could serve it. In a strange way, he became something of a popular hero, since many people enjoyed the idea that he had fooled the Nazis. His story also taught museums an uncomfortable lesson: an expert's eye, however well trained, can be deceived when it wants to see a masterpiece.
exercises.question: According to the passage, van Meegeren mixed Bakelite into his paints ----.
options: to produce the blue colour that Vermeer had used
so that the paint would dry fast and look very old
to protect the paintings from damage during the war
because museum experts had recommended it to him
because it was cheaper than the oils Vermeer used
exercises.explanation: Parçaya göre Bakelit boyanın birkaç saatte kurumasını ve üç yüz yıllık boya gibi sert ve çatlak görünmesini sağladı: ‘so that the paint would dry fast and look very old’. Mavi pigment (‘blue colour’) ayrı bir bulgudur; savaşta korunma (‘protect’), uzman tavsiyesi (‘recommended’) ve ucuzluk (‘cheaper’) parçada geçmez.

exercises.question: It can be inferred from the passage that van Meegeren confessed mainly because ----.
options: he wanted to give the money back to the Nazi official
scientists had already proved that the painting was a fake
the museum demanded that he return the painting it had bought
a forgery conviction was far less serious than a conviction for treason
he had already painted a "Vermeer" in front of witnesses
exercises.explanation: Van Meegeren vatana ihanetle suçlanıyordu; tabloyu kendisinin yaptığını itiraf edince sahtecilikten yargılandı ve yalnızca bir yıl ceza aldı. exercises.question: According to the last sentence, the lesson museums learned was that ----.
options: paintings should never be sold to foreign officials
scientific tests are less reliable than an expert's eye
even skilled experts may be fooled if they are eager to find a great work
only paintings older than three hundred years are valuable
forgers should receive much longer prison sentences
exercises.explanation: Son cümle, ne kadar eğitimli olursa olsun bir uzmanın gözünün bir başyapıt görmek istediğinde aldanabileceğini söyler: ‘even skilled experts may be fooled …’. Yabancı yetkililere satış (‘foreign officials’) ve cezaların uzunluğu (‘longer prison sentences’) dersle ilgili değildir; testlerin daha az güvenilir olduğu (‘less reliable’) parçanın tersidir, çünkü vakayı testler çözdü; üç yüz yıllık tablolar (‘older than three hundred’) hakkında da böyle bir yargı yoktur.

exercises.passage: In a dry lake bed in Death Valley, California, hundreds of rocks lie at the end of long tracks in the mud, as if they had been dragged across the ground. Some of the rocks weigh more than 300 kilograms, and their trails can be hundreds of metres long. Yet for most of the twentieth century, nobody had ever seen one move. Visitors suggested all kinds of explanations, from strong winds to magnetic fields, and some even blamed tourists playing tricks. Geologists themselves disagreed. Some believed that the wind alone could push the rocks when the mud was wet and slippery, while others argued that the stones must be frozen into sheets of ice. The mystery was finally solved in 2014 by a team led by a palaeobiologist and his cousin, an engineer. They placed GPS devices in several rocks and set up a weather station and cameras nearby. Patience was essential, because the conditions they were waiting for do not occur every year. During one winter, a shallow pond formed on the lake bed and froze overnight into thin panels of ice. When the sun began to melt the ice the next day, light winds broke it into large pieces, which slowly pushed the rocks forward at a few metres per minute. The movement was so slow that it was barely visible to the human eye. The researchers later admitted that they had been lucky, since they had expected to wait for years before seeing a single stone move.
exercises.question: The passage mainly deals with ----.
options: why tourists are no longer allowed to visit Death Valley
the effects of climate change on lakes in California
the history of GPS technology in geological research
how strong winds create deep tracks in dry mud
how scientists finally explained the movement of rocks across a desert lake bed
exercises.explanation: Parça Death Valley'deki kayaların nasıl hareket ettiği gizemini ve 2014'te nasıl çözüldüğünü anlatır: ‘how scientists finally explained the movement of rocks …’. Turist yasağı (‘no longer allowed’) ve iklim değişikliği (‘climate change’) parçada yoktur; GPS (‘history of GPS’) yalnızca kullanılan bir araçtır; güçlü rüzgârlar (‘strong winds’) ise çürütülen açıklamalardan biridir.

magnetic fields under the lake bed

the rocks only moved while they were frozen into the ground
the tracks had been made thousands of years earlier
the movement was rare and too slow to notice easily
earlier geologists had shown no interest in the rocks

nodes.title: Diyalog, restatement, paragraf
nodes.description: Sorgu diyalogları, yakın anlam, paragraf tamamlama ve anlamı bozan cümle

exercises.passage:
Inspector: Where were you between eight and ten last night?
Mr Hale: ----
Inspector: Can anyone confirm that you were there the whole time?
Mr Hale: Yes, the waiter will remember me; I argued with him about the bill.
exercises.question: Diyalogdaki boşluğa hangisi getirilmelidir?
options: I have never been to that part of the city before.
I usually go to bed early on weekdays.
Why do you want to know about my car?
I'm afraid I can't remember who the waiter was.
I was having dinner at the Italian restaurant on King Street.
exercises.explanation: Müfettiş ‘Can anyone confirm that you were there the whole time?’ diye soruyor; yani boşlukta belirli bir yer söylenmeli. Bay Hale'in garsondan söz etmesi bunun bir restoran olduğunu gösterir: ‘I was having dinner at the Italian restaurant …’. ‘never been to that part’ bir yer vermez; ‘go to bed early’ genel bir alışkanlıktır; ‘my car’ soruyla ilgisizdir; garsonu hatırlamadığını söylemek (‘can't remember’) son repliğiyle çelişir.

exercises.passage:
Sara: The museum says the stolen vase was insured for two million euros.
Tom: ----
Sara: Exactly, and the owner was in serious debt before the robbery.
Tom: Then we should check his bank records first.
exercises.question: Diyalogdaki boşluğa hangisi getirilmelidir?
options: I don't think vases are worth stealing at all.
That's a lot of money. Maybe someone had a reason to want it stolen.
Has the thief been caught yet?
The museum will reopen next week.
I've always preferred modern art to old vases.
exercises.explanation: Sara ‘Exactly’ diyerek Tom'un fikrine katılıyor ve sahibinin borçlu olduğunu ekliyor; Tom'un birinin vazonun çalınmasını isteyebileceğini ima etmesi gerekir: ‘That's a lot of money. Maybe someone had a reason …’. Vazoların çalınmaya değmediği (‘worth stealing’) ‘Exactly’ ile desteklenemez; hırsızın yakalanması (‘caught’) bir sorudur ve ‘Exactly’ ile yanıtlanmaz; müzenin açılması (‘reopen’) ve modern sanat zevki (‘modern art’) konuyla bağlantısızdır.

exercises.passage:
Journalist: Your team has finally identified the bones found under the car park. How did you do it?
Scientist: ----
Journalist: So the living relatives helped you solve the puzzle?
Scientist: Yes. Without them, we could never have been certain.
exercises.question: Diyalogdaki boşluğa hangisi getirilmelidir?
options: We simply guessed from the age of the car park.
Nobody has studied the bones yet.
The car park will be closed for another year.
We compared DNA from the bones with samples from two of his living descendants.
We found his name carved on a stone nearby.
exercises.explanation: Gazeteci ‘So the living relatives helped you …?’ diye özetliyor; demek ki bilim insanı yaşayan akrabalardan söz etmiş olmalı: ‘We compared DNA … with samples from two of his living descendants.’ Tahmin etmek (‘guessed’) akrabalarla ilgili değildir; kemiklerin incelenmediği (‘Nobody has studied’) kimliğin belirlendiğiyle çelişir; otoparkın kapanması (‘closed’) soruyu yanıtlamaz; taştaki isim (‘carved’) de akrabalardan söz etmez.

exercises.question:
Verilen cümleye anlamca en yakın cümle hangisidir?

The thief could hardly have entered the house without someone noticing him.
options: It is very unlikely that the thief entered the house unnoticed.
Someone noticed the thief as soon as he had left the house.
The thief found it easy to enter the house because nobody was at home.
Nobody could have stopped the thief from entering the house.
The thief was hardly ever noticed by people in the neighbourhood.
exercises.explanation: ‘could hardly have entered … without someone noticing’ hırsızın fark edilmeden girmiş olmasının neredeyse imkânsız olduğunu söyler: ‘It is very unlikely that the thief entered the house unnoticed.’ ‘as soon as he had left’ girişi çıkışa çevirir; ‘found it easy’ anlamı tersine çevirir; ‘Nobody could have stopped’ başka bir yargıdır; ‘hardly ever noticed’ ise ‘hardly’ sözcüğünü farklı bir anlamda kullanır.

exercises.question:
Verilen cümleye anlamca en yakın cümle hangisidir?

It was only after the detective had read the letter again that he noticed the hidden message.
options: The detective noticed the hidden message the moment he first read the letter.
Having noticed the hidden message, the detective decided not to read the letter again.
The detective did not notice the hidden message until he read the letter a second time.
The detective read the letter again because someone had told him about the hidden message.
The hidden message was so clear that the detective noticed it immediately.
exercises.explanation: ‘It was only after … that’ gizli mesajın ancak mektup yeniden okunduktan sonra fark edildiğini vurgular: ‘… did not notice the hidden message until he read the letter a second time.’ ‘the moment he first read’ ve ‘so clear … immediately’ mesajın hemen fark edildiğini söyler; ‘decided not to read’ sıralamayı bozar; ‘someone had told him’ ise cümlede olmayan bir neden ekler.

exercises.question:
Verilen cümleye anlamca en yakın cümle hangisidir?

Despite having a strong alibi, the suspect was kept in custody for two more days.
options: Because his alibi was strong, the suspect was released after two days.
The suspect was kept for two days until he could prove his alibi.
The suspect's alibi was so weak that he had to stay in custody.
The suspect had no alibi, so the police let him go two days later.
Although the suspect had a strong alibi, he was held for another two days.
exercises.explanation: ‘Despite having a strong alibi’ karşıtlık bildirir: güçlü bir mazereti olmasına rağmen iki gün daha tutuldu: ‘Although the suspect had a strong alibi, he was held for another two days.’ ‘Because … released’ karşıtlığı nedene çevirir; ‘until he could prove’ cümlede olmayan bir koşul ekler; ‘so weak’ ve ‘had no alibi’ ise mazeretin güçlü olduğu bilgisiyle çelişir.

exercises.passage: When a body is found outdoors, one of the first questions investigators ask is how long the person has been dead. Surprisingly, insects can often provide the answer. ---- Because these flies develop through stages at a predictable speed, which depends mainly on the temperature, experts can estimate the time of death by studying the age of the young insects they collect. This method is especially useful when several days have passed and other medical signs are no longer reliable.
exercises.question: Paragrafta boş bırakılan yere hangisi getirilmelidir?
options: Many insects are useful to farmers because they eat harmful pests.
Certain flies arrive within minutes of death and lay their eggs on the body.
Most detectives receive little training in biology.
Cold weather usually keeps people indoors in winter.
Butterflies are among the most colourful insects in the world.
exercises.explanation: Boşluktan sonraki cümle ‘these flies’ diye başlar; önceki cümlede sineklerden söz edilmiş olmalı: ‘Certain flies arrive within minutes of death and lay their eggs on the body.’ Çiftçilere yararlı böcekler (‘farmers’), dedektiflerin eğitimi (‘training’), soğuk hava (‘indoors’) ve kelebekler (‘Butterflies’) ölüm zamanının tahmin edilmesiyle bağ kurmaz ve ‘these flies’ ifadesini açıklamaz.

exercises.passage: Dogs have been used to track missing people for centuries, and their success is no accident. A dog's nose contains up to 300 million scent receptors, compared with about six million in a human nose. ---- As a result, a trained dog can follow a person's trail even several days after he or she has walked past. Some police forces now also train dogs to find specific items, such as banknotes or electronic devices.
exercises.question: Paragrafta boş bırakılan yere hangisi getirilmelidir?
options: However, dogs are not allowed in most shopping centres.
Cats, by contrast, are rarely kept as pets in large cities.
Unfortunately, most people prefer small dogs to large ones.
In addition, the part of its brain that analyses smells is around forty times larger than ours.
For this reason, dogs need to be walked at least twice a day.
exercises.explanation: Paragraf köpeklerin koku alma gücünü burun alıcılarıyla açıklıyor; boşluktan sonra ‘As a result’ ile iz sürme başarısı geliyor. Bu yüzden ikinci bir koku avantajı eklenmeli: ‘In addition, the part of its brain that analyses smells …’. Alışveriş merkezi yasağı (‘shopping centres’), kediler (‘Cats’), küçük köpek tercihi (‘prefer small dogs’) ve günlük yürüyüş (‘walked’) koku alma yeteneğiyle ilgili değildir.

exercises.passage: During the First World War, the young Agatha Christie worked in a hospital pharmacy, where she learned a great deal about medicines and poisons. ---- In her novels, more than thirty victims die from poison, and the symptoms she described were so accurate that doctors and pharmacists praised her books. In 1977, a nurse in London even recognised the signs of thallium poisoning in a sick child after reading one of Christie's stories, and the child's life was saved.
exercises.question: Paragrafta boş bırakılan yere hangisi getirilmelidir?
options: This knowledge later became one of the most useful tools in her writing career.
She also enjoyed travelling by train across Europe.
Hospitals at that time were often short of trained nurses.
Her first husband was a pilot in the Royal Flying Corps.
Many readers find her detective stories difficult to follow.
exercises.explanation: Önceki cümle Christie'nin eczanede ilaç ve zehirler hakkında çok şey öğrendiğini, sonraki cümle ise romanlarında zehirlenmeleri doğru anlattığını söyler; aradaki bağı kuran cümle bu bilginin yazarlığına yaradığıdır: ‘This knowledge later became one of the most useful tools …’. Tren yolculukları (‘travelling’), hemşire eksikliği (‘nurses’), ilk eşi (‘husband’) ve okurların zorlanması (‘difficult to follow’) bu bağı kurmaz.

exercises.passage: (I) The Phaistos Disc, a clay disc found on Crete in 1908, is covered on both sides with stamped symbols arranged in a spiral. (II) Because no other text in the same script has been discovered, linguists have had very little material to compare it with. (III) Some scholars have argued that the symbols record a religious song, while others see them as a calendar or a list of goods. (IV) The disc is now displayed in a museum in Heraklion, where it attracts thousands of visitors every year. (V) A few researchers even suspect that it is a modern forgery, although most experts accept that it is genuine.
exercises.question: Paragrafta anlam bütünlüğünü bozan cümle hangisidir?
options: I
II
III
IV
V
exercises.explanation: Paragraf Phaistos Diski’nin çözülmesi ve ne anlama geldiği üzerine yapılan tartışmaları anlatır. ‘IV’ numaralı cümle de diskten söz eder ama bu tartışmadan ayrılıp diskin bugün nerede sergilendiğine geçer. ‘I’ konuyu açar, ‘II’ karşılaştırma malzemesinin azlığını, ‘III’ farklı yorumları, ‘V’ ise sahte olabileceği görüşünü vererek akışı sürdürür.

exercises.passage: (I) The stories of Sherlock Holmes, first published in 1887, had a surprising influence on real police work. (II) Holmes examined footprints, tobacco ash and soil samples at a time when most police forces still relied mainly on confessions. (III) Several early forensic scientists, including the Frenchman Edmond Locard, said that the stories had encouraged them to study physical evidence. (IV) Today, many forensic textbooks still mention Holmes as an early example of scientific investigation. (V) Arthur Conan Doyle, who created the detective, was also a keen sportsman who played cricket and football.
exercises.question: Paragrafta anlam bütünlüğünü bozan cümle hangisidir?
options: I
II
III
IV
V
exercises.explanation: Paragraf Sherlock Holmes öykülerinin gerçek polis çalışmasına etkisini anlatır. ‘V’ numaralı cümle de Holmes'un yaratıcısından söz eder ama konuyu yazarın spor merakına kaydırır. ‘I’ etkiyi tanıtır, ‘II’ Holmes'un fiziksel kanıt incelemesini, ‘III’ Locard gibi bilim insanlarına ilham verişini, ‘IV’ ise bugünkü ders kitaplarındaki yerini anlatarak akışı sürdürür.

exercises.passage: (I) Even when a criminal's face is hidden, investigators may still be able to identify him by the way he walks. (II) Each person has a slightly different gait, which depends on the length of the legs, the shape of the hips and old injuries. (III) Walking for thirty minutes a day is one of the simplest ways to stay healthy. (IV) Experts compare security camera footage of a suspect with videos of known individuals, measuring details such as stride length and arm movement. (V) Although courts in several countries have accepted this kind of evidence, critics warn that it is less reliable than DNA or fingerprints.
exercises.question: Paragrafta anlam bütünlüğünü bozan cümle hangisidir?
options: I
II
III
IV
V
exercises.explanation: Paragraf suçluların yürüyüş biçiminden tanınmasını anlatır. ‘III’ numaralı cümle de yürümekten söz eder ama kimlik belirlemeden ayrılıp yürüyüşün sağlığa yararına geçer. ‘I’ konuyu açar, ‘II’ her insanın yürüyüşünün neden farklı olduğunu, ‘IV’ uzmanların görüntüleri nasıl karşılaştırdığını, ‘V’ ise bu kanıtın mahkemelerdeki yerini ve eleştirileri anlatır.

nodes.title: Ünite testi
nodes.description: 15 karışık soru; geçmek için %80 doğru yap

exercises.question: After weeks of careful work, the detectives finally managed to ---- the leaked documents back to a single computer in the finance office.
options: yield
burst
trace
occupy
freeze
exercises.explanation: Sızdırılan belgelerin kaynağını bir bilgisayara kadar geri izlemek ‘trace … back to’ kalıbıyla anlatılır: ‘trace’. ‘yield’ (ürün/sonuç vermek), ‘burst’ (patlamak), ‘occupy’ (işgal etmek, yer kaplamak) ve ‘freeze’ (donmak, dondurmak) ‘back to’ ile bu anlamı vermez.

exercises.question: The court found the young man ----, as the evidence clearly showed that he had been abroad when the crime took place.
options: guilty
domestic
elderly
native
innocent
exercises.explanation: Suç işlendiğinde yurt dışında olduğu kanıtlanan kişi suçsuz bulunur: ‘innocent’. ‘guilty’ (suçlu) kanıtla çelişir; ‘domestic’ (yerli, ev içi), ‘elderly’ (yaşlı) ve ‘native’ (yerli, ana dili olan) mahkeme kararını anlatmaz.

exercises.question: Two of the paintings that the gang stole from the gallery in 2019 ---- in a farmhouse last spring.
options: discovering
were discovered
having been discovered
to be discovered
which were discovered
exercises.explanation: Öznesi ‘Two of the paintings’ olan cümlede ‘that the gang stole … in 2019’ sıfat cümlesidir; ana cümleye çekimli bir yüklem gerekir ve tablolar bulunur (edilgen): ‘were discovered’. ‘discovering’ ve ‘having been discovered’ fiilimsidir; ‘to be discovered’ tek başına yüklem olamaz; ‘which were discovered’ ise ikinci bir sıfat cümlesi kurup cümleyi yüklemsiz bırakır.

exercises.question: ---- the alarm went off at midnight, nobody in the building called the police.
options: Because
Unless
So that
Although
In case
exercises.explanation: Alarmın çalması ile kimsenin polisi aramaması arasında karşıtlık var: ‘Although’ (-e rağmen). ‘Because’ mantıksız bir neden kurar; ‘Unless’ (-mezse) geçmişteki gerçek bir olaya uymaz; ‘So that’ amaç, ‘In case’ ise önlem bildirir.

exercises.passage: Before photography became common, the police had no reliable way of recording what criminals looked like. In the 1880s, a French clerk named Alphonse Bertillon developed a system (1)---- eleven body measurements, such as the length of the head and of the left foot, were written on a card for every prisoner.
exercises.question: (1) numaralı boşluk için en uygun ifadeyi seçin.
options: in which
which
who
that
what
exercises.explanation: Boşluktan sonraki cümle (‘eleven body measurements … were written’) kendi öznesi ve yüklemi olan tam bir cümledir; ‘system’ sözcüğünü “o sistemde” anlamıyla bağlamak için ‘in which’ gerekir. ‘which’ ve ‘that’ cümlede eksik bir öğe olmasını ister, oysa eksik öğe yok; ‘who’ insan içindir; ‘what’ ise önünde isim olan bir sıfat cümlesi kurmaz.

exercises.question: ----, the witness would have recognised the man who took her bag.
options: If the street lights are repaired soon
Because she had forgotten her glasses at home
If the street had not been so dark
Although the man was wearing a mask
Unless the police show her some photographs
exercises.explanation: ‘would have recognised’ üçüncü tip koşulun ana cümlesidir; ‘if’ cümlesi past perfect ister: ‘If the street had not been so dark’. ‘are repaired soon’ ve ‘Unless … show’ birinci tip koşula aittir; ‘forgotten her glasses’ tanıyamamanın nedenidir, tanımayı açıklamaz; ‘Although … mask’ ise ‘would have’ ile mantıklı bir karşıtlık kurmaz.

exercises.question: The fingerprints on the glass did not belong to the owner of the house, ----.
options: so the owner must have touched it
unless the owner had touched it
although they were clearly his own
because they matched his own perfectly
which suggested that someone else had been in the kitchen
exercises.explanation: Parmak izleri ev sahibine ait değilse bu başka birinin mutfakta bulunduğunu düşündürür: ‘which suggested that someone else had been in the kitchen’. ‘must have touched’, ‘matched his own’ ve ‘clearly his own’ izlerin ev sahibine ait olmadığı bilgisiyle çelişir; ‘unless the owner’ anlamsız bir koşul kurar.

exercises.question:
Aşağıdaki İngilizce cümlenin anlamca en yakın Türkçe karşılığı hangisidir?

The detective suspected that the letter had been written by someone who knew the family well.
options: Dedektif, aileyi iyi tanıdığı için mektubu kimin yazdığını hemen anladı.
Dedektif, mektubun aileyi iyi tanıyan biri tarafından yazıldığından şüpheleniyordu.
Mektubu yazan kişi, dedektifin aileyi iyi tanıdığından şüpheleniyordu.
Dedektif, aileden birinin mektubu okuduğunu kesin olarak biliyordu.
Aile, mektubu dedektifin yazdığından şüphelenmeye başlamıştı.
exercises.explanation: ‘suspected that the letter had been written by someone who knew the family well’ öğeleri ‘…aileyi iyi tanıyan biri tarafından yazıldığından şüpheleniyordu.’ cümlesindedir. ‘hemen anladı’ şüpheyi kesinliğe çevirir; ‘Mektubu yazan kişi’ şüphelenen kişiyi değiştirir; ‘okuduğunu’ yazmayı okumaya çevirir; ‘Aile’ ile başlayan cümle ise şüpheyi aileye ve yazarı dedektife verir.

exercises.question:
Aşağıdaki Türkçe cümlenin anlamca en yakın İngilizce karşılığı hangisidir?

Kayıp tablonun nerede saklandığını yalnızca iki kişi biliyordu.
options: Two people were hiding the missing painting in a place nobody could find.
Only two people were asked where the missing painting had been found.
Nobody understood why two people had hidden the painting.
Only two people knew where the missing painting was hidden.
The missing painting was hidden by two people who knew each other.
exercises.explanation: ‘nerede saklandığını yalnızca iki kişi biliyordu’ öğesi ‘Only two people knew where the missing painting was hidden.’ cümlesinde karşılanır. ‘were hiding’ iki kişiyi saklayan yapar; ‘were asked’ bilmeyi sorulmaya çevirir; ‘Nobody understood why’ nerede yerine neden sorar; ‘each other’ ise iki kişinin birbirini tanıdığını ekler.

exercises.passage: In 1903, a prisoner named Will West arrived at Leavenworth prison in Kansas. To the clerks' astonishment, his body measurements were almost identical to those of another prisoner, William West, who was already there, and the two men even looked alike. Only their fingerprints were clearly different. The case is often told to show why fingerprints, rather than body measurements, became the standard way of identifying criminals.
exercises.question: According to the passage, the Will West case is important because ----.
options: it showed that fingerprints were more reliable than body measurements
the two prisoners had committed exactly the same crime
it proved that the clerks at Leavenworth made many mistakes
it led to the closing of the prison in Kansas
body measurements were taken there for the first time
exercises.explanation: Parçaya göre iki mahkûmun vücut ölçüleri neredeyse aynıydı, yalnızca parmak izleri farklıydı; olay parmak izinin ölçülerden daha güvenilir olduğunu gösterir: ‘it showed that fingerprints were more reliable …’. Aynı suç (‘same crime’), memurların hataları (‘mistakes’) ve hapishanenin kapanması (‘closing’) parçada yoktur; ölçülerin ilk kez alınması (‘first time’) da söylenmez.

exercises.passage: In 1903, a prisoner named Will West arrived at Leavenworth prison in Kansas. To the clerks' astonishment, his body measurements were almost identical to those of another prisoner, William West, who was already there, and the two men even looked alike. Only their fingerprints were clearly different. The case is often told to show why fingerprints, rather than body measurements, became the standard way of identifying criminals.
exercises.question: It can be inferred from the passage that before this case ----.
options: fingerprints were the only method used in prisons
the two men had worked together as clerks
body measurements were used to identify prisoners
prisoners were not allowed to have their photographs taken
William West had already been released from prison
exercises.explanation: Memurların ölçülerin neredeyse aynı olmasına şaşırması, mahkûmların o dönemde vücut ölçüleriyle tanımlandığını gösterir: ‘body measurements were used to identify prisoners’. Parmak izinin tek yöntem olduğu (‘only method’) olayın ders verdiği bilgiyle çelişir; memur olarak çalışmak (‘worked together’) ve fotoğraf yasağı (‘photographs’) parçada geçmez; William West'in serbest bırakılması (‘released’) ise onun zaten orada olduğu bilgisiyle çelişir.

exercises.passage:
Officer: We found the suspect's car abandoned near the river.
Detective: ----
Officer: No, the keys were still inside and the engine was warm.
Detective: Then he can't have gone far.
exercises.question: Diyalogdaki boşluğa hangisi getirilmelidir?
options: Has the river been cleaned recently?
I'm sure he has already left the country.
Where did you park your own car?
The car was bought only last year, wasn't it?
Did he take the keys with him?
exercises.explanation: Polis memuru ‘No, the keys were still inside …’ diye yanıt veriyor; boşlukta anahtarlarla ilgili bir soru olmalı: ‘Did he take the keys with him?’ Nehrin temizlenmesi (‘river’) ve memurun kendi arabası (‘park your own car’) konuyla ilgisizdir; şüphelinin ülkeyi terk ettiği (‘left the country’) dedektifin son sözüyle çelişir; arabanın ne zaman alındığı (‘bought’) da anahtar yanıtıyla uyuşmaz.

exercises.question:
Verilen cümleye anlamca en yakın cümle hangisidir?

Hardly anyone believed the old woman's story until the police found the stolen jewels in her neighbour's garage.
options: Everyone believed the old woman's story, so the police searched the neighbour's garage.
Few people believed the old woman's story before the jewels were found in her neighbour's garage.
The old woman found the stolen jewels in her neighbour's garage and hid them.
The neighbour told the police a story that nobody believed.
The police did not find the jewels because nobody believed the old woman.
exercises.explanation: ‘Hardly anyone believed … until …’ mücevherler bulunana kadar neredeyse kimsenin kadına inanmadığını söyler: ‘Few people believed the old woman's story before the jewels were found …’. ‘Everyone believed’ anlamı tersine çevirir; ‘hid them’ mücevherleri bulanı ve saklayanı kadın yapar; ‘The neighbour told’ hikâyeyi komşuya verir; ‘did not find’ ise mücevherlerin bulunduğu bilgisiyle çelişir.

exercises.passage: Investigators examining a crime scene today must be extremely careful not to leave their own traces. ---- For this reason, they wear protective suits, gloves, masks and shoe covers, and every person who enters the area is recorded. Even so, mistakes happen: in one well-known German case, police spent years searching for a female criminal whose DNA appeared at dozens of crime scenes, only to discover that it belonged to a factory worker who had packed the cotton swabs.
exercises.question: Paragrafta boş bırakılan yere hangisi getirilmelidir?
options: Most crimes are committed by people who know their victims.
Protective suits are usually made in large factories in Asia.
Many young people dream of becoming crime scene investigators.
Modern DNA tests are so sensitive that a single hair or a drop of sweat can confuse the results.
Fingerprints were first used by police in the late nineteenth century.
exercises.explanation: Önceki cümle araştırmacıların kendi izlerini bırakmaması gerektiğini, sonraki cümle ise ‘For this reason’ ile koruyucu giysileri anlatır; arada bu dikkatin nedeni gelmelidir: ‘Modern DNA tests are so sensitive …’. Suçluların kurbanlarını tanıması (‘victims’), giysilerin üretildiği yer (‘Asia’), gençlerin hayalleri (‘dream’) ve parmak izinin tarihi (‘nineteenth’) ‘For this reason’ bağlantısını kurmaz.

exercises.passage: (I) On a Monday morning in 1911, the Mona Lisa disappeared from the Louvre in Paris. (II) The thief, an Italian worker named Vincenzo Peruggia, had hidden inside the museum and walked out with the painting under his coat. (III) Leonardo da Vinci, who painted it in the early sixteenth century, was also a talented engineer who designed flying machines. (IV) For more than two years the painting was missing, and crowds came to the museum just to look at the empty space on the wall. (V) Peruggia was finally caught in Florence when he tried to sell it to an art dealer.
exercises.question: Paragrafta anlam bütünlüğünü bozan cümle hangisidir?
options: I
II
III
IV
V
exercises.explanation: Paragraf Mona Lisa'nın 1911'de çalınmasını ve bulunmasını anlatır. ‘III’ numaralı cümle de tablodan söz eder ama hırsızlık olayından ayrılıp ressamın mühendislik yeteneğine geçer. ‘I’ olayı açar, ‘II’ hırsızın yöntemini, ‘IV’ tablonun kayıp kaldığı yılları, ‘V’ ise hırsızın Floransa'da yakalanmasını anlatarak akışı tamamlar.

nodes.title: Ünite ödülü
nodes.description: Üniteyi bitir, bonus XP kazan

nodes.title: Yarım deneme 2
nodes.description: YDS dağılımında 40 soru, 90 dakika (B1+–B2). Planın 22. haftasındaki yarım deneme; sonucunu önceki denemelerle karşılaştır.

exercises.question: Volunteers spent two years trying to ---- the old steam locomotive, which had been left to rust in a field for more than half a century.
options: resemble
exceed
restore
impose
consult
exercises.explanation: Paslanmaya terk edilmiş eski bir lokomotif için yapılacak iş onu ‘restore’ etmek (eski hâline getirmek) olur. ‘resemble’ (benzemek) çaba gerektiren bir iş değildir; ‘exceed’ (aşmak) bir sınır ya da miktar ister; ‘impose’ (dayatmak) kural ya da vergi için kullanılır; ‘consult’ (danışmak) ise bir kişi ya da kaynakla kullanılır, lokomotifle değil.

exercises.question: Because the early symptoms of the disease are often rather ----, doctors may need several tests before they can make a firm diagnosis.
options: superior
voluntary
compact
lawful
vague
exercises.explanation: Kesin tanı için birkaç test gerekiyorsa belirtiler belirsizdir: ‘vague’ (belirsiz, bulanık). ‘superior’ (üstün) bir karşılaştırma ister; ‘voluntary’ (gönüllü) belirtiler için anlamsızdır; ‘compact’ (sıkı, küçük ve derli toplu) eşyalar için kullanılır; ‘lawful’ (yasal) ise hukukla ilgilidir.

exercises.question: The council decided to ---- work on the new stadium after it became clear that the costs would be far higher than the original budget.
options: halt
verify
inspire
portray
absorb
exercises.explanation: Maliyetler bütçeyi çok aşınca yapılacak şey çalışmayı ‘halt’ etmek (durdurmak) olur. ‘verify’ (doğrulamak) bir bilgi ya da iddia ister; ‘inspire’ (ilham vermek) mantığa uymaz; ‘portray’ (tasvir etmek) bir resim ya da anlatım için kullanılır; ‘absorb’ (emmek, içine çekmek) ise inşaat işiyle anlam kurmaz.

exercises.question: The first public railway to use steam locomotives, which opened between Stockton and Darlington in 1825, ---- coal as well as passengers in its early years.
options: carrying
to carry
having carried
carried
which carried
exercises.explanation: Öznesi ‘The first public railway’ olan cümlede ‘which opened … in 1825’ araya giren bir yan cümledir; boşluğa çekimli bir ana fiil gerekir: ‘carried’. ‘carrying’ ve ‘having carried’ çekimsiz fiilimsilerdir; ‘to carry’ tek başına yüklem olamaz; ‘which carried’ ise ikinci bir yan cümle kurar ve cümleyi yine ana fiilsiz bırakır.

exercises.question: By the time the rescue team reached the village, most of the residents ---- to higher ground.
options: have already moved
had already moved
will already move
are already moving
already move
exercises.explanation: ‘By the time … reached’ geçmişte bir an verir; ondan önce tamamlanmış bir eylem için ‘past perfect’ gerekir: ‘had already moved’. ‘have already moved’ şimdiki zamana bağlanır; ‘will already move’ gelecek zamandır; ‘are already moving’ ve ‘already move’ ise geçmişteki bir anla uyuşmayan şimdiki zaman biçimleridir.

exercises.question: If the city ---- more money in public transport ten years ago, traffic would not be so heavy today.
options: invests
would invest
has invested
will invest
had invested
exercises.explanation: Geçmişteki bir koşul (‘ten years ago’) bugünkü bir sonucu (‘would not be … today’) etkiliyor; bu karma koşul cümlesi ‘If’ kısmında ‘past perfect’ ister: ‘had invested’. ‘invests’ ve ‘will invest’ birinci tip koşula aittir; ‘has invested’ ‘ten years ago’ ile kullanılamaz; ‘would invest’ ise ‘If’ yan cümlesine girmez.

exercises.question: ---- its small size, the ant is able to carry objects many times heavier than its own body.
options: Despite
Although
Because of
Unless
So that
exercises.explanation: Küçük boyut ile ağır yük taşıma arasında zıtlık vardır ve boşluktan sonra bir isim öbeği (‘its small size’) gelir; bu yüzden ‘Despite’ doğrudur. ‘Although’ zıtlık bildirir ama ardından tam bir cümle ister; ‘Because of’ neden bildirir, anlamı bozar; ‘Unless’ ve ‘So that’ da cümle ister ve koşul ya da amaç anlamı taşır.

exercises.question: After the match, the coach explained to the players ---- they needed to rest for at least two days before training again.
options: which
whose
why
whom
what
exercises.explanation: Boşluktan sonra eksiksiz bir cümle (‘they needed to rest …’) geliyor ve antrenör dinlenmenin nedenini açıklıyor; isim cümleciği ‘why’ ile kurulur. ‘which’ ve ‘what’ cümlede eksik bir öğenin yerini tutar, burada eksik öğe yoktur; ‘whose’ ardından bir isim ister; ‘whom’ ise nesne konumundaki bir kişi için kullanılır.

exercises.passage: For most of history, people relied on drying, salting and smoking to keep food from going bad. In 1795, however, the French government, which needed a better way to (1)---- its armies with food during long campaigns, offered a large prize for a new method. A confectioner named Nicolas Appert spent almost fifteen years on the problem. He discovered that if food was sealed in glass bottles and then heated in boiling water, it would stay fresh for months. (2)----, he could not explain why his method worked, since bacteria had not yet been identified as the cause of decay. Appert finally won the prize in 1810, and his technique was quickly (3)---- by a British merchant who replaced the fragile glass with tin cans. Early cans were so thick that they had to be opened with a hammer, and the can opener was not invented until almost fifty years later. It was only in the 1860s that Louis Pasteur showed that heat kills the tiny organisms (4)---- for spoiling food, which finally explained Appert's success. Today, canned food is so common that we rarely think about it; (5)----, it was once regarded as a remarkable achievement of science.
exercises.question: (1) numaralı boşluğa hangisi gelmelidir?
options: acquire
supply
prohibit
deposit
resist
exercises.explanation: Hükümet ordularına yiyecek sağlamanın daha iyi bir yolunu arıyordu; ‘supply somebody with something’ (bir şeyle donatmak, sağlamak) kalıbı ‘its armies with food’ yapısına uyar. ‘acquire’ (edinmek) bu kalıpla kullanılmaz; ‘prohibit’ (yasaklamak) anlamca terstir; ‘deposit’ (yatırmak, bırakmak) ve ‘resist’ (direnmek) ise ordulara yiyecek vermeyi anlatmaz.

exercises.passage: For most of history, people relied on drying, salting and smoking to keep food from going bad. In 1795, however, the French government, which needed a better way to (1)---- its armies with food during long campaigns, offered a large prize for a new method. A confectioner named Nicolas Appert spent almost fifteen years on the problem. He discovered that if food was sealed in glass bottles and then heated in boiling water, it would stay fresh for months. (2)----, he could not explain why his method worked, since bacteria had not yet been identified as the cause of decay. Appert finally won the prize in 1810, and his technique was quickly (3)---- by a British merchant who replaced the fragile glass with tin cans. Early cans were so thick that they had to be opened with a hammer, and the can opener was not invented until almost fifty years later. It was only in the 1860s that Louis Pasteur showed that heat kills the tiny organisms (4)---- for spoiling food, which finally explained Appert's success. Today, canned food is so common that we rarely think about it; (5)----, it was once regarded as a remarkable achievement of science.
exercises.question: (2) numaralı boşluğa hangisi gelmelidir?
options: Therefore
For instance
Similarly
However
In addition

exercises.passage: On warm summer evenings in many parts of the world, fields and forests are lit up by thousands of tiny flashing lights. These lights are produced by fireflies, which are not actually flies but beetles. The light is created by a chemical reaction inside a special organ in the insect's body, and it is remarkably efficient: almost all of the energy is released as light rather than heat. For a long time, scientists assumed that the flashes were mainly a warning to predators that fireflies taste unpleasant. Although this is partly true, research has shown that their main purpose is communication between males and females. Each species has its own pattern of flashes, which differs in length, colour and rhythm. Males fly through the air sending signals, while females, which usually wait on plants or grass, respond with a flash of their own if they recognise the right pattern. In some species, however, this system is exploited in a rather cruel way. Females of one group, known as Photuris, copy the signals of other species, and when a male of that species lands nearby, they catch and eat him. Today, many firefly populations appear to be declining, although reliable data are still limited. The loss of wetlands and grassland is thought to be one cause, and the widespread use of pesticides is another. Researchers are particularly concerned about artificial light, which is increasing in almost every region. Street lamps and brightly lit buildings can make it difficult for fireflies to see each other's signals, so fewer of them find a partner. Some towns have responded by switching off the lights in parks during the breeding season, and early results suggest that such simple measures may make a real difference.
exercises.question: The passage is mainly concerned with ----.
options: the chemical process that allows beetles to produce heat
the reasons why some insects taste unpleasant to predators
how fireflies use light to communicate and why their numbers may be falling
the history of street lighting in towns and cities
the physical differences between flies and beetles
exercises.explanation: Metin ateşböceklerinin ışığı eşleriyle iletişim için nasıl kullandığını ve sayılarının neden azalıyor olabileceğini anlatır: ‘how fireflies use light to communicate and why their numbers may be falling’. Işık neredeyse hiç ısı (‘heat’) üretmez; yırtıcılara karşı tadın kötü olması (‘unpleasant’) yalnızca kısmen doğru bir ayrıntıdır; sokak lambalarının tarihi (‘history’) anlatılmaz; sinek ile böcek farkı (‘physical differences’) ise tek cümlelik bir bilgidir.

exercises.passage: For decades, athletes and ordinary gym users were told that they should always stretch before exercise. The traditional routine, in which a muscle is slowly pulled and held in one position for thirty seconds or more, was believed to prevent injuries and to improve performance. Coaches repeated this advice so often that few people thought to question it. Since the late 1990s, however, a growing body of research has challenged this assumption. Several large studies, some of which followed thousands of army recruits during their training, found that those who stretched before exercise suffered almost as many injuries as those who did not. Even more surprisingly, laboratory experiments suggested that holding a stretch for a long time can temporarily reduce the strength of a muscle, which may be a disadvantage in sports that require speed or power, such as sprinting or jumping. As a result, many sports scientists now recommend a different kind of preparation. Instead of standing still, athletes are encouraged to perform a dynamic warm-up, in which they move their joints through a full range of motion while gradually raising their heart rate. Light jogging, leg swings and gentle jumps are typical examples. This does not mean that traditional stretching is useless. It can still increase flexibility when it is done regularly, and it may be valuable after training or as part of a separate session. The problem, researchers argue, lies mainly in its timing. It is worth remembering, though, that many of the studies involved fairly small groups, and the effects they measured were often modest. For most people who exercise for pleasure, the difference between the two methods is probably small, and any warm-up is better than none.
exercises.question: What is the main idea of the passage?
options: Research has changed expert views on how athletes should prepare for exercise.
Stretching after training is more dangerous than stretching before it.
Army recruits are injured more often than professional athletes.
Sprinters need more strength than athletes in any other sport.
People who exercise for pleasure should never stretch their muscles.
exercises.explanation: Metin, araştırmaların egzersiz öncesi hazırlık konusundaki uzman görüşlerini nasıl değiştirdiğini anlatır: ‘Research has changed expert views on how athletes should prepare for exercise.’ Antrenman sonrası esnemenin daha tehlikeli (‘dangerous’) olduğu söylenmez, tersine yararlı olabilir; askerlerle profesyonel sporcuların karşılaştırılması (‘recruits’) yapılmaz; sprintçilerin gücü (‘Sprinters’) yalnızca örnektir; ‘never stretch’ ise metnin sonundaki ılımlı görüşle çelişir.

The traditional routine, in which a muscle is slowly pulled and held in one position for thirty seconds or more, was believed to prevent injuries and to improve performance. Coaches repeated this advice so often that few people thought to question it. Since the late 1990s, however, a growing body of research has challenged this assumption. Several large studies, some of which followed thousands of army recruits during their training, found that those who stretched before exercise suffered almost as many injuries as those who did not. Even more surprisingly, laboratory experiments suggested that holding a stretch for a long time can temporarily reduce the strength of a muscle, which may be a disadvantage in sports that require speed or power, such as sprinting or jumping. As a result, many sports scientists now recommend a different kind of preparation. Instead of standing still, athletes are encouraged to perform a dynamic warm-up, in which they move their joints through a full range of motion while gradually raising their heart rate. Light jogging, leg swings and gentle jumps are typical examples. This does not mean that traditional stretching is useless. It can still increase flexibility when it is done regularly, and it may be valuable after training or as part of a separate session. The problem, researchers argue, lies mainly in its timing. It is worth remembering, though, that many of the studies involved fairly small groups, and the effects they measured were often modest. For most people who exercise for pleasure, the difference between the two methods is probably small, and any warm-up is better than none.
exercises.question: The author's attitude towards the new research on stretching can best be described as ----.
options: completely dismissive
openly hostile
uncritically enthusiastic
indifferent
generally accepting but aware of its limitations
exercises.explanation: Yazar yeni bulguları aktarır ve genel olarak kabul eder, ama çalışmaların küçük gruplarla yapıldığını ve etkilerin sınırlı olduğunu da hatırlatır: ‘generally accepting but aware of its limitations’. Bulguları benimsediği için ‘completely dismissive’ ve ‘openly hostile’ uymaz; sınırlılıklara dikkat çektiği için ‘uncritically enthusiastic’ de yanlıştır; konuyu ayrıntılı tartıştığından ‘indifferent’ de değildir.

exercises.passage:
Emre: I read that the city plans to close the old tram line next year.
Laura: ----
Emre: That's true, but buses would need far less maintenance than the old tracks.
exercises.question: Diyalogdaki boşluğa hangisi getirilmelidir?
options: Yes, the new trams are expected to arrive next spring.
Do you know how much a monthly ticket costs now?
The council has decided to extend the line to the airport.
What a shame! Thousands of people still rely on it to get to work.
I have never understood why trams are so noisy.
exercises.explanation: Emre ‘That's true, but …’ diyerek Laura'nın hattın kapanmasına karşı öne sürdüğü bir gerekçeyi kabul edip otobüslerin avantajını söyler; bu gerekçe binlerce kişinin hâlâ hatta güvendiğidir: ‘What a shame! Thousands of people still rely on it to get to work.’ Yeni tramvaylar (‘spring’) ve hattın uzatılması (‘airport’) hattın kapanmasıyla çelişir; aylık bilet sorusu (‘monthly’) ‘That's true’ ile yanıtlanmaz; tramvayların gürültüsü (‘noisy’) ise ‘but’ ile kurulan karşıtlığa uymaz.

exercises.passage:
Coach: Your times have been getting slower for three weeks now. How many hours are you sleeping?
Selin: ----
Coach: That's not nearly enough. Your body repairs itself during sleep, so you need at least eight hours.
exercises.question: Diyalogdaki boşluğa hangisi getirilmelidir?
options: About five or six, because I've been studying late for my exams.
I've been training twice a day, just as you suggested.
My new running shoes are much lighter than the old ones.
I usually sleep for about nine hours, sometimes even ten.
I think the track is slower when it's raining.
exercises.explanation: Antrenör kaç saat uyuduğunu soruyor ve yanıtın ‘hiç yeterli olmadığını’ söylüyor; bu yüzden kısa bir uyku süresi gerekir: ‘About five or six, because I've been studying late for my exams.’ Günde iki antrenman (‘twice’) ve yeni ayakkabılar (‘shoes’) soruyu yanıtlamaz; dokuz-on saat (‘nine hours’) sekiz saatten fazladır, ‘not nearly enough’ ile çelişir; yağmurlu pist (‘raining’) ise uyku sorusuyla ilgisizdir.

exercises.passage:
Ayşe: Did you know that termites build mounds that stay cool even in the desert heat?
Mark: ----
Ayşe: Exactly. Some architects have already copied the idea to design buildings that need less air conditioning.
exercises.question: Diyalogdaki boşluğa hangisi getirilmelidir?
options: I've always been afraid of insects, especially large ones.
Yes, but termites cause serious damage to wooden houses.
Really? I suppose engineers could learn something from that.
Deserts are usually very cold at night.
How long do termites usually live?
exercises.explanation: Ayşe ‘Exactly’ diyerek Mark'ın söylediğini onaylar ve mimarların bu fikri kopyaladığını ekler; demek ki Mark mühendislerin bundan bir şey öğrenebileceğini söylemiştir: ‘Really? I suppose engineers could learn something from that.’ Böcek korkusu (‘afraid’) ve ahşap evlere zarar (‘damage’) mimarların fikri kopyalamasıyla bağlantı kurmaz; çöldeki gece soğuğu (‘cold at night’) konuyu değiştirir; ömür sorusu (‘How long’) ise ‘Exactly’ ile yanıtlanamaz.

exercises.question:
Verilen cümleye anlamca en yakın cümle hangisidir?

No sooner had the athletes crossed the finish line than heavy rain began to fall.
options: The athletes crossed the finish line just before the race was cancelled because of the rain.
Heavy rain had been falling for a long time before the athletes finished the race.
The athletes were unable to finish the race because of the heavy rain.
Although heavy rain was falling, the athletes managed to cross the finish line quickly.
Heavy rain started to fall immediately after the athletes crossed the finish line.
exercises.explanation: ‘No sooner had … than’ bir olayın hemen ardından ötekinin geldiğini anlatır: sporcular bitiş çizgisini geçer geçmez yağmur başladı (‘Heavy rain started to fall immediately after …’). Yarışın iptal edilmesi (‘cancelled’) cümlede yoktur; ‘for a long time before’ sıralamayı tersine çevirir; ‘unable to finish’ sporcuların bitirdiği bilgisiyle çelişir; ‘Although … was falling’ ise yağmurun yarış sırasında yağdığını söyler.

exercises.question:
Verilen cümleye anlamca en yakın cümle hangisidir?

The railway would never have been built if local merchants had not provided most of the money.
options: Local merchants refused to pay for the railway, so it was never built.
It was only because local merchants paid most of the costs that the railway could be built.
The railway was built without any financial help from local merchants.
Local merchants became rich because the railway had been built.
If the railway had been built, local merchants would have provided the money.
exercises.explanation: Üçüncü tip koşul cümlesi gerçekte olanın tersini anlatır: tüccarlar paranın çoğunu verdi ve demiryolu bu sayede yapıldı (‘It was only because local merchants paid most of the costs …’). ‘refused … never built’ ve ‘without any financial help’ gerçekte olanı tersine çevirir; tüccarların zenginleşmesi (‘became rich’) cümlede yoktur; ‘If the railway had been built …’ ise koşul ile sonucun yerini değiştirir.

exercises.passage: Wooden pagodas in Japan have survived powerful earthquakes for centuries, even though many stone buildings around them collapsed. ---- When the ground shakes, the floors move in opposite directions, a little like a snake, and the energy of the earthquake is gradually absorbed. A thick central pillar, which is not fixed firmly to the floors, also helps to keep the structure stable. Modern engineers have studied these principles when designing tall buildings in earthquake zones.
exercises.question: Paragrafta boş bırakılan yere hangisi getirilmelidir?
options: Most pagodas were built to store religious objects rather than to house people.
Japan experiences more than a thousand small earthquakes every year.
Wood is a cheaper building material than stone in most countries.
The secret lies in their design: each storey rests loosely on the one below rather than being tightly connected to it.
Many tourists visit these pagodas during the spring festival.
exercises.explanation: Boşluktan sonraki cümle katların ters yönlerde hareket ettiğini anlatır; bu, katların birbirine gevşekçe oturduğunu söyleyen bir açıklama bekler: ‘The secret lies in their design: each storey rests loosely on the one below …’. Dini eşyaların saklanması (‘religious’), yıllık deprem sayısı (‘thousand’), ahşabın ucuzluğu (‘cheaper’) ve bahar festivalindeki turistler (‘tourists’) pagodaların neden yıkılmadığını açıklamaz.

exercises.passage: When the world's first underground railway opened in London in 1863, its trains were pulled by steam locomotives. ---- To reduce the problem, the tunnels were built close to the surface, and openings were left at regular intervals so that the smoke could escape. Even so, passengers often complained about the dirty air, and some doctors claimed that the journey was harmful to health. It was only when electric trains were introduced in the 1890s that deeper tunnels became practical.
exercises.question: Paragrafta boş bırakılan yere hangisi getirilmelidir?
options: This meant that the tunnels quickly filled with smoke and steam.
Within its first year, the line carried more than nine million passengers.
The tickets were cheap enough for working people to afford.
Many other cities, such as Paris and New York, later built their own systems.
At first, the line was only about six kilometres long.
exercises.explanation: Boşluktan sonra gelen ‘To reduce the problem’ bir sorunun daha önce söylenmesini gerektirir; bu sorun tünellerin duman ve buharla dolmasıdır: ‘This meant that the tunnels quickly filled with smoke and steam.’ Yolcu sayısı (‘million’), ucuz biletler (‘tickets’), başka kentlerdeki sistemler (‘Paris’) ve hattın uzunluğu (‘kilometres’) bir sorun bildirmez, dolayısıyla ‘the problem’ ile bağlanamaz.

exercises.passage: (I) In the early nineteenth century, an American businessman named Frederic Tudor began cutting ice from frozen lakes in New England and shipping it to hot countries. (II) Many people laughed at the idea, since they believed the ice would melt long before it reached its destination. (III) Today, most households keep their food fresh in electric refrigerators, which use far less energy than older models. (IV) Tudor, however, found that ice packed tightly in sawdust could survive voyages of several months. (V) By the 1850s, his company was sending ice as far as India, where it was used to cool drinks and keep food fresh.
exercises.question: Paragrafta anlam bütünlüğünü bozan cümle hangisidir?
options: I
II
III
IV
V
exercises.explanation: Paragraf Frederic Tudor'un gölden kestiği buzu sıcak ülkelere taşıma girişimini anlatır. ‘III’ numaralı cümle de yiyecekleri soğuk tutmaktan söz eder ama Tudor'un ticaretinden ayrılıp bugünkü buzdolaplarının enerji tüketimine geçer. ‘I’ girişimi başlatır, ‘II’ insanların kuşkusunu, ‘IV’ buzun talaş içinde korunduğunu, ‘V’ ise işin Hindistan'a kadar büyüdüğünü anlatarak akışı sürdürür.

exercises.passage: (I) Desert locusts usually live alone and avoid one another, much like ordinary grasshoppers. (II) After heavy rains, however, plenty of vegetation grows, and their numbers increase rapidly. (III) When the insects are crowded together, they begin to change colour and behaviour, and they start moving in large groups. (IV) These groups can form swarms containing billions of locusts, which may travel more than a hundred kilometres a day and destroy crops across entire regions. (V) In some countries, locusts are cooked and eaten, as they are rich in protein.
exercises.question: Paragrafta anlam bütünlüğünü bozan cümle hangisidir?
options: I
II
III
IV
V
exercises.explanation: Paragraf çöl çekirgelerinin yalnız yaşayan böceklerden nasıl dev sürülere dönüştüğünü adım adım anlatır. ‘V’ numaralı cümle de çekirgelerden söz eder ama bu süreçten ayrılıp çekirgelerin besin olarak yenmesine geçer. ‘I’ başlangıç durumunu, ‘II’ yağmurdan sonra sayının artmasını, ‘III’ kalabalıkta davranış değişikliğini, ‘IV’ ise oluşan sürülerin verdiği zararı anlatır.

exercises.passage: (I) Many endurance athletes spend several weeks training at high altitude before important competitions. (II) Mountain climbing has become an increasingly popular hobby, and some climbers now pay large sums to reach the highest peaks. (III) Because the air contains less oxygen at altitude, the body responds by producing more red blood cells. (IV) When the athletes return to sea level, these extra cells allow their muscles to receive more oxygen, at least for a few weeks. (V) However, the benefits vary greatly between individuals, and some athletes show almost no improvement.
exercises.question: Paragrafta anlam bütünlüğünü bozan cümle hangisidir?
options: I
II
III
IV
V

exercises.passage: (I) Before the second half of the nineteenth century, few buildings were more than five or six storeys high. (II) One reason was that people were unwilling to climb so many stairs every day. (III) The safety elevator invented by Elisha Otis, which would not fall even if its cable broke, removed this obstacle. (IV) Otis died in 1861, and his sons took over the family business. (V) Together with the development of steel frames, the elevator made it possible to construct the first skyscrapers in cities such as Chicago and New York.

options: I
